newsitem.title: ITALY: FORECAST-Italy April PPI seen subdued before rise.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST-Italy April PPI seen subdued before rise.

text.p: Italian PPI and WPI data due out next week are expected to show price pressures remained contained in April but for producer prices this could be the last month they show such low annual growth, analysts said.
Wholesale prices are seen posting a negative yearly rate.
The two indicators will be released at 0700 GMT on June 16.
A Reuter survey of 10 economists showed April PPI rising 0.2 percent month on month and by 1.0 percent year on year. In March the rises were 0.3 and 0.9 percent respectively.
Wholesale prices are seen posting a 0.2 percent monthly rise but showing a year on year fall of 0.1 percent. March WPI fell 0.2 percent month on month but posted an annual rise of 0.3 percent.
"The April PPI figure is positive even if in coming months the unfavourable statistical comparison will push the year on year rate towards two percent," said Paolo Casadio of Credito Italiano.
Analysts said that subdued commodity prices and particularly a fall in the cost of oil, would help producer prices.

For wholesale prices, Lucia Trevisan of Caboto noted that the comparison with March 1996 WPI had a positive effect on the year on year data because the "mad cow" impact in March last year was one of the main factors behind a monthly rise of 0.7 percent while the yearly increase was 4.5 percent.
However, analysts expect only a modest rise in April WPI which should result in a negative year on year figure.
"I expect to see contained levels until mid-year, then the rate will tend to rise and the annual average increase should be 0.9 percent," said Trevisan.
